findings: Root cause: config/production.env sets CACHE_TTL_SECONDS=0, and loadConfig's merge order (`{...base, ...override}`) applies it after base.env's 300, silently overriding the documented 300s TTL and disabling caching entirely in production.

The override originated as an explicitly temporary debug change (commit titled "debug: temporarily disable cache to reproduce issue #412") made eight months ago and was never reverted — there is no expiry mechanism or tracking for temporary debug config flags.
The debug cache-disable was bundled into the same commit as an unrelated, intentional DB_POOL_SIZE change, making the commit non-atomic and harder to safely review, isolate, or revert.

Nothing in production.env or configLoader.ts marks the override as a debug artifact rather than intentional configuration, so it reads as valid production config to anyone not checking git blame/history.

Internal docs assert a 300-second TTL, but nothing in the config loading path validates or alerts on divergence between documented expected values and actual effective config, letting the 0-second override drift undetected for 8 months.

loadConfig performs an unchecked, unlogged shallow merge of base and override files with no diffing or reporting of which keys were overridden, so there is no visibility into effective vs. base configuration at load time.
With caching fully disabled, every cache-eligible request has been falling through to the backing store in production for 8 months — a sustained, unnoticed availability/performance risk.
